title: Universal quantifier branching
statement: Let $q$ be a finite Boolean quantifier prefix, $\varphi$ a CNF formula, and $k,S\in\mathbb{N}$. If $k$ is a valid index in $q$ and its $k$th bit is false, then the valuation predicate at $(k,S)$ holds exactly when it holds at both $(k+1,2S)$ and $(k+1,2S+1)$.
hypotheses_covered: A CNF formula φ over ℕ-indexed variables
k is less than the length of q
The bit of q at index k is false
